_note: Diagnoses of dead ends, kept OUT of the job checkpoints. A driver rewrites its whole checkpoint on every save, so an entry added by hand while the job is running is silently clobbered -- which is what happened to the pthr2 entry on 2026-10-24. Nothing but the audit writes this file.

pthr2.why: Not usable at GFN2-xTB. In the relaxed trans conformer the amide C=O is 1.306 A and C-N 1.455 A (single bonds) against 1.235/1.332 in ala, thr, ser and the monoanion pthr1. The dianion delocalises its excess charge into the carbonyl, so the pi system whose rotation the barrier measures is already broken, and the barrier comes out at 9.94 kcal/mol against 16-20 for every other model and 14-24 from experiment. The phosphorylation effect is taken from the monoanion.

pser2.why: The other phosphate dianion, expected to fail exactly as pthr2 does and for the same reason. Entered in advance so the expected failure is not reported as a new fault; if it passes the checks, this entry is simply unused.

cis_trans_comparison.why: The cis/trans energy differences are NOT usable, except for thr. Relaxing the two minima independently let them settle into different intramolecular hydrogen-bond networks: ala trans has N-H...O 1.91 and cis has none; pthr1 trans has two and cis has none; ser cis gains one; pser1 swaps its acceptor. Only thr keeps the same two bonds in both. The resulting "phosphorylation effect" came out +6.70 kcal/mol for Thr and -5.87 for Ser -- opposite signs for the same chemical change on near-identical molecules, which is how the fault announced itself. What is measured is the hydrogen bond, not the amide. thr alone is sound: matched conformers, a converged saddle with one imaginary mode at 61i, a barrier of 21.38 (xTB) and 18.52 (DFT) inside the measured 14-24, and cis-trans +0.46 (xTB) / -0.39 (DFT).

relay.why: The sum of the two hops is a degenerate coordinate: across all 26 points C5-H never left 1.09-1.15 A, so the +12.12 kcal/mol maximum is the cost of protonating Glu58, not the abstraction. Superseded by the stepwise stage.

stepwise.why: 4 monotonic runs rather than 2 because of one 0.27 kcal/mol dip on the rise at xi1 = -1.40, well inside the 1.5 bound on a reversal within a run. The profile is otherwise a clean barrier: +9.83 to +47.51 at xi1 = 0.00 (C5-H 1.35, H...O 1.35, symmetric) and down to +16.76. The stored scan_drop = 13.25 and bond_CH = 1.81/1.99 records come from superseded tests: the 13.25 is the descent from the barrier, and the long C5-H distances are the proton having transferred (H...O 1.01 and 0.99). Both checks have been replaced -- segment_drop for the profile, proton_bonded for the hydrogen.

ss.why: GFN2-xTB puts the symmetric arrangement of this displacement 8-9 kcal/mol BELOW the reactant complex, so the hypervalent trichalcogen anion comes out a bound species and the surface is a well where it must be a barrier. Measured first on ss, where thiolate-disulfide exchange is known to be second order with a real barrier, so the shape is wrong and not merely the number. Same over-stabilisation of a thiolate that Manuscript 2 found at the semiempirical level. chalcogen_barrier and exchange_well report it directly; scan_drop and exchange_segments are consequences, because a nearly flat well has wobbles at the step size and a barrierless exothermic profile such as s_se is monotonic rather than the two runs a displacement should show. Consequence: no saddle search can be seeded from this surface and the DFT stage must build its own symmetric guess. The scans are kept because showing the failure is systematic across all six systems is itself the result. Note this does NOT cover scan_hysteresis, which was a real fault of ours and is fixed: the backward sweep now starts from where the forward sweep arrived instead of from a constructed product, and se_s went from 46.27 to 2.91 kcal/mol.
